meta.provenance_line: Figures are illustrative while we wire live data.
meta._note: SEED for the cell-page spine dev surface (a trade in a place). Illustrative London restaurant economics; wire to the real cell data layer + finance engines (cells.ts, net_profit, breakeven) on promotion. Numbers must then match across surfaces. ALL user-visible prose lives here (verdicts, notes, myth, reads) so scaled pages read trade-and-place specific. related: per-sibling keep-% removed 2026-07-11 (rulebook v1 section 5, net margin by trade in a specific city is unknowable); each sibling now carries cost_to_open_usd, the modeled index-100 startup-capital archetype (src/lib/markets/startup_capital_archetypes.ts), hospitality-adjacent order, cafe first, no dental on a restaurant page (rulebook v1 section 32).
meta._identity: TRUST ARITHMETIC (every figure below closes these): rev = covers/wk x spend x 52 (315 x $38 x 52 = $622K, stated $620K); owner take = keeps% x rev ($620K x 7% = $43K); break-even covers/day = daily fixed / contribution per cover, with variable 66% / fixed 27% / keep 7% of sales: ($620K x 27% / 365) / ($38 x 34%) = 36 of a 45-cover typical day; payback = cost to open / annual take ($197K / $43K = 55 months). Subtype rows close the same identities at their own spend, covers and capex.

headline.answer: A demanding trade in a deep market: high turnover, thin take-home.
headline.spread_line: Turnover runs from $280K to $1.4M a year, typically about $620K.

_meta._note: gross/operating removed (Final Ascent P2): they contradicted the $100 split (food 31 implies ~69 gross, not 64; operating 16 never reconciled). money_split.items is now the ONE margin source; the owner-keeps waterfall derives from it.

verdict.break_in_line: This is one of the harder trades to enter here. Rent, wages and food cost leave a thin slice, so the operators who last run tight rotas and a sharp menu.
verdict.crowded_line: A new room competes for covers from day one.

money_split.surface_line: Wages and food cost eat two thirds of every $100 before rent is even paid.
money_split.read: Wages and food are two thirds of every dollar; the operators who last claw two or three points back from each, because the 7% at the end is all that is left to pay the owner.

subtypes._identity: Per format: rev = spend x covers/day x 365; take = keeps% x rev; break-even covers/day = utilization x typical covers (74% / 80% / 85%, from each format's fixed share over its contribution ratio); payback months = cost to open / take x 12 (31 / 55 / 102). Full service IS the page's blended typical case.
subtypes.thesis: The blended answer hides three different businesses. Pick the one you mean.
subtypes.hint: The leaner the format, the more the owner keeps and the easier it is to break in.

items.name: Fast casual
items.note: Counter service, tight menu, fast covers; the kindest format to break into.

items.name: Full service
items.note: Table service, full kitchen and floor; the blended typical case.

items.name: Fine dining
items.note: High spend per head, but labour and fit-out are heavy; thin keep, hard entry.

demand._identity: 315 covers/wk x $38 a head x 52 weeks = $622K, matching headline.rev_p50_usd ($620K); about 45 covers a typical day.
demand.surface_line: Weekends and evenings carry the week; weekday lunch is the trade you fight for.
demand.channel_line: Most spend is still eaten in the room; delivery is a supplement, not the business.
demand.catchment_note: Office workers are the anchor here; the others fill the shoulders of the week.

who_suits.subtitle: Suits a hands-on operator with kitchen or floor experience and capital to carry a slow first year, not a passive investor.
who_suits._pos_note: Coarse honesty steps only: 20 = Low, 50 = Mid, 80 = High. Words carry the read; positions never fake precision.

myth.subtitle: A dramatic first-year collapse is not what actually closes most rooms.
myth.claim: Nine in ten restaurants fail in the first year.
myth.reality: The real first-year survival rate is nearer three in four. Most closures come later and quietly, when a rent review or a bad winter meets a take-home that was always thin, not from a dramatic opening-year collapse.

survival.line: Survivors, not failures: most rooms are still trading at year one.

cost_drivers.name: Wages
cost_drivers.note: Kitchen and front-of-house are the biggest line; rota tightly.

cost_drivers.name: Food cost
cost_drivers.note: Menu engineering and waste control move the gross line most.

cost_drivers.name: Rent & rates
cost_drivers.note: A prime address eats margin before you serve a cover.

owner._identity: take = keeps% x rev: $620K x 7% = $43K a year.
owner.surface_line: Large turnover, thin keep: most of every sales dollar is spent before it reaches the owner.

break_even._identity: 36 covers = daily fixed / contribution per cover = ($620K x 27% / 365 = $459) / ($38 x 34% = $12.92); 36 of 45 typical covers = 80% of a typical day. The page swaps BOTH numbers per picked format from subtypes.items, so this line must stay format-neutral.
break_even.surface_line: A quiet Tuesday is the real test, not a busy Friday: break-even is set by the fixed costs, not the weekend rush.

wages.surface_line: The head chef sets the pay ceiling; everyone else clusters below.

setup._identity: payback = cost to open / annual owner take: full service $197K / $43K = 55 months. The page DERIVES payback from the picked format's capex and take (no stored payback field), so the figure can never contradict the picker.
setup.surface_line: About $197K to open the doors, most of it fit-out and kitchen; at a typical take it pays back in about four and a half years.

seasonality.surface_line: December carries the year; the new-year lull is when cash gets thin.

nearby.surface_line: London turns over the most but keeps the least per dollar; the smaller cities are easier to break into.

risks.surface_line: Cost shocks, not quiet nights, are what close most kitchens.

items.name: Food and energy inflation
items.note: The single most cited pressure; a hard winter compounds it.

items.name: Staff turnover
items.note: Rehiring and retraining eat both margin and service quality.

items.name: Rent reviews
items.note: A five-year review can reset the biggest fixed cost overnight.

items.name: Demand swings
items.note: A quiet January or a transport strike lands straight on cash.

close.bottom_line: Deep demand and real turnover, with a thin slice left at the end: this trade rewards operators who control costs daily.
